attribution.note: Zitron states both assertions in his own voice.

semantics.note: Read at publication, the normalization preserves both assertions. The commercial clause assesses evidence then available; it does not firmly predict that only Nvidia will profit.

contract.note: The frontier-training scope follows the surrounding discussion. Assessing contemporary indications of future profit, including benefits to users, fairly reflects the commercial clause without requiring realized profits.

evidence.note: Contemporary small-model research demonstrates useful synthetic training data, but does not establish data sufficiency for frontier successors.
Contemporary experiments demonstrate limits to repeated data, alongside benefits from limited repetition. They do not establish that all data-generation methods are inadequate.
Available before publication, this research demonstrates a mitigation for model collapse. It does not establish sufficient generated data for the contemplated frontier training.

Klarna's contemporary disclosure provides a concrete indication of prospective profit outside Nvidia. It remains a company projection; this single example does not settle whether such indications were scant.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes neither frontier data sufficiency nor its impossibility. Synthetic-data successes and collapse mitigation qualify the pessimistic account without settling it. Klarna supplies relevant commercial counterevidence, but one company projection does not establish whether substantial indications of future profit existed by publication. Neither assertion is resolved.
